item.title: My reverse proxy: separating provisioning, configuration and health checks
item.description:
My reverse-proxy project runs Caddy in Docker on a DigitalOcean VPS, with Cloudflare DNS in front. Terraform creates the infrastructure, Ansible configures it, and a set of checks looks at the resulting service.

This article describes the configuration as I reviewed it in October and November 2026. The source is private, so the diagram and excerpts are simplified and contain no real domains, addresses or credentials. I read the code without running a deployment, so the findings below are about what the code does, not about measured incidents.

item.title: Making Caddy, AWS EC2, CloudWatch, Step Functions, and Lambda Work Together
item.description: I already ran Caddy at home for Home Assistant. This article is the AWS edge version: a t4g.nano EC2 instance, automatic HTTPS, JSON access logs shipped to CloudWatch by a nightly Python script, and a Step Functions workflow that runs two Lambda functions over those logs. The goal was cheap visibility into a personal reverse proxy, not a SaaS dashboard bill.

item.title: Networking evolution — building a home network lab
item.description: Cloud bills pushed me toward a home lab: old PCs, Docker instead of SaaS where possible, and enough scripting to rebuild after a bad weekend. This post is how that network grew — not a perfect design, but one that taught routing, VPNs, and virtualization by breaking things locally.
